mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations for industrial sector firms and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 6-month moving averages signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a recovery in the housing market, which boosts construction-related sector earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.4%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.
